key_insight: Translation-invariant topological CSS codes decouple into stacks of higher-form toric codes exactly when superlattice translations act trivially on every excitation layer and interlayer gluing vanishes.
engineering_relevance: This criterion and an explicit circuit-construction algorithm provide a systematic way to simplify higher-dimensional quantum error-correcting codes for fault-tolerant computing.
method: Organize excitations into dimensional superselection layers and identify translation action and interlayer gluing.
For prime-p qudits with m nonzero layers and finitely many excitation types per layer, remove gluing by further coarse-graining by p^(m−1) in every direction once translations act trivially.
Construct a finite-depth, local, CSS-preserving Clifford decoupling circuit using SUM and SWAP gates, possibly with ancillas.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports an exact decoupling theorem, a coarse-graining bound, and a constructive algorithm, but no numerical benchmarks or hardware evaluation.
watch_item: The coarse-graining factor can grow rapidly with the number of excitation layers, and practical circuit and ancilla overheads are not quantified in the abstract.
paper_title: Toric codes all the way down: decoupling translation-invariant topological CSS codes in higher dimensions
